title: Data in transit could be intercepted and used to identify parent
description: During parent registration, sensitive data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) is transmitted from ExternalEntity EE1 to Process P1. If intercepted, this data could be used to identify the parent user.

title: Data in transit could be intercepted and disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) transmitted from EE1 to P1 could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal information.

title: Authentication Service may collect excessive data beyond minimum required
description: The Authentication Service (P1) may store and process more data than necessary for authentication purposes, including government ID and six-digit code, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: Authentication Service may use registration data for unauthorized purposes
description: The Authentication Service (P1) may use the collected registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) for purposes beyond authentication, such as marketing, profiling, or sharing with third parties without consent.

title: Authentication Service may fail to comply with data protection regulations
description: The Authentication Service (P1) may not properly comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding collection, storage, and processing of sensitive personal data including government ID and six-digit code.

title: Unauthorized access to stored parent account data
description: The MongoDB users collection (DS1) stores parent account data that could be accessed by unauthorized parties if proper access controls are not implemented, leading to disclosure of personal data.

title: Data integrity compromise of stored parent account data
description: The stored parent account data in MongoDB could be tampered with or modified by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity.

title: Identification through stored parent account data
description: Parent account data contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individuals, potentially leading to privacy violations if accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Linkability of JWT tokens in transit
description: JWT tokens transmitted in the data flow contain metadata and claims that could be used to link multiple requests to the same user, enabling correlation of activities across sessions.

title: Identification of parent user via JWT payload
description: The JWT token payload contains user identifiers that could be used to identify the parent user to unauthorized observers intercepting the data flow.

title: Usurpation via intercepted JWT tokens
description: JWT tokens transmitted in transit could be intercepted and reused by attackers to impersonate the authenticated user, gaining unauthorized access to the parent user's services.

title: Disclosure of user data in transit
description: User data transmitted alongside the JWT token could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of personal information.

title: Parent email and password shared by child user
description: Child user (EE2) shares parent email and password with authentication service, creating identifiability risk as parent's email directly identifies the parent and links to child's account
assumptions: Child has access to parent credentials and shares them during login

title: Data in transit could be intercepted and linked
description: Parent email and password transmitted in flow DF4 could be intercepted, with metadata about the parties (child user, authentication service) used to link the data to specific individuals
assumptions: Transmission is not fully encrypted or metadata is exposed

title: Authentication service may store or disclose parent credentials
description: Authentication service (P1) receives and processes parent email and password, creating risk of improper storage, unauthorized access, or disclosure of sensitive credential data
assumptions: Service may not have adequate security controls for credential storage

title: Authentication service could be compromised allowing credential misuse
description: If authentication service is compromised, parent credentials could be misused to access child's account or other services, enabling identity usurpation
assumptions: Service has vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Identifiable child data shared from authentication service
description: The authentication service (P1) shares JWT tokens and child profiles containing personally identifiable information about the child user. This act of sharing identifiable data at the source creates a privacy threat as the data is inherently linked to a specific individual.

title: Identifiable data in transit during authentication flow
description: JWT tokens and child profiles transmitted in the data flow (DF5) contain identifying information about the child user. Data in transit is vulnerable to interception, which could expose identifying metadata and profile information.

title: Potential for identity usurpation at child user endpoint
description: The child user (EE2) receives JWT tokens that could potentially be misused for identity usurpation if the token is compromised or shared with unauthorized parties. The destination element processes the data in a way that creates this risk.

title: Linking via Government ID in Transit
description: Government ID transmitted in the data flow can be used to link this child's profile data to other databases or records, enabling creation of comprehensive profiles across systems.
assumptions: The government ID is a unique identifier that can be matched across systems

title: Identification via Sensitive Personal Data in Transit
description: The combination of name, DOB, gender, and government ID in transit can uniquely identify the child, creating identification risks during data transmission.
assumptions: These data elements together form a unique identifier for the child

title: Child Unaware of Data Collection
description: The child (data subject) is not directly involved in the profile creation process and may not be aware that their sensitive personal data is being collected and processed.
assumptions: The child lacks capacity to consent to data collection

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Child Data Processing
description: Processing of child's government ID and personal data may violate regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K which impose strict requirements for children's data protection and parental consent.
assumptions: Applicable data protection regulations require specific safeguards for children's data

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties due to insufficient access controls, violating the minimality principle and exposing sensitive personal information about children.
assumptions: MongoDB collection lacks proper access controls or authentication mechanisms

title: Identification Through Data in Transit
description: Child profile data transmitted from process P3 to data store DS2 could be intercepted, allowing identification of children through the collected personal data.
assumptions: Data transmission lacks encryption or is transmitted over unsecured channels

title: Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: Child profile data in transit could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through network interception or man-in-the-middle attacks.
assumptions: Data flow lacks proper encryption (e.g., TLS) during transmission

title: Unauthorized Profile Modification
description: Process P3 may not properly authenticate or authorize before storing/updating child profiles, allowing unauthorized actors to modify sensitive child information.
assumptions: Process lacks proper authentication/authorization checks before data operations

title: Child Identifiability in Video Data
description: Child users share video content, search queries, likes, and comments that can directly identify them. Video metadata (timestamps, location, device info) combined with personal content creates high identifiability risk.

title: Linkability via Video Metadata
description: Video metadata (timestamps, device identifiers, IP addresses) in transit can be used to link a child's activity across different services and time periods, creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection
description: Video Management Service processes child personal data (videos, comments, search history) which requires special protections under COPPA, GDPR-K, and other child privacy regulations. Improper management could lead to regulatory violations.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 from context applies to improper personal data management; child data context makes this particularly relevant.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Video Content
description: Video content, comments, and personal data stored by the Video Management Service could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms.

title: Child Account Usurpation
description: Child users may share credentials or be impersonated by others, allowing unauthorized access to their video content, search history, and personal data.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, device IDs, user IDs, etc.) can contain or be used to identify individuals. When stored in transit or at the data flow level, this metadata may be exposed or used for identification purposes.
assumptions: Video metadata typically contains identifying or quasi-identifying information that can be used to link to individuals.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node I.1.2 from context [3] as it directly addresses identified information in metadata.

title: Inappropriate storage of video data and metadata
description: Storing video files and metadata in MongoDB collection DS3 may result in unauthorized access or disclosure of personal data. The storage boundary may not adequately protect the data from internal or external access.
assumptions: MongoDB collection may be accessible to authorized personnel or systems that could lead to unintended disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard data disclosure node; the exact disclosure risk depends on MongoDB access controls which are not specified.

title: Video data integrity compromised during storage
description: Video files and metadata stored in DS3 could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted, affecting data integrity and potentially leading to misinformation or unauthorized modification.
assumptions: Storage system may not have adequate integrity controls or audit mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard data integrity node; actual risk depends on MongoDB configuration and access controls.

title: Unnecessary Storage of Child Search and Watch History
description: Storing children's search and watch history in MongoDB represents a data disclosure that may be avoidable. This personal data about children's interests and behaviors is collected and stored, potentially exceeding what is strictly necessary for the system's core functionality.
assumptions: The system could potentially operate without storing detailed search/watch history, or could use anonymized/aggregated data instead.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 from context as it covers data disclosure across boundaries; the exact node may vary in different LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Identification Risk from Search and Watch History
description: Child search and watch history data can be used to identify the child or infer sensitive information about their interests, preferences, and potentially their location or activities. This data is inherently identifiable and could be linked to other data sources.
assumptions: Search and watch history contains enough detail to potentially identify or profile the child.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a reasonable node for identification threats; may need adjustment based on specific data granularity.

title: Linkability of Child Activity Patterns
description: Stored search and watch history can be used to link different activities, sessions, or data points about the child, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of their behavior and interests that could be exploited or misused.
assumptions: Multiple data points from search and watch history can be correlated to build a profile.
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a standard node for linkability threats; the specific node may vary.

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Children's Data
description: Storing children's search and watch history may violate regulations such as COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act), GDPR-K (GDPR for children), or other child-specific privacy regulations that impose strict requirements on data collection, storage, and processing of minors' personal data.
assumptions: The system operates in jurisdictions with child privacy regulations; the data qualifies as personal data of children under applicable laws.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a reasonable node for non-compliance threats; specific regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction.

title: User shares identifiable video content
description: Parent User uploads video that inherently contains personally identifiable information (PII) such as facial features, location context, or activities that can identify the user or others in the video.

title: Video data in transit can be intercepted and linked
description: Video data flowing from EE1 to P2 may be intercepted by third parties, and metadata (timestamps, device info) could be used to link the video to the user's identity.

title: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Video Management Service may store, process, or share video data with third parties without proper authorization, leading to unauthorized disclosure of personal data.

title: Non-compliant video data management practices
description: Video Management Service may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding video data retention, access controls, or user consent for video processing.

title: Video stream contains identifiable personal data in transit
description: The video stream transmitted from the Video Management Service to the child user may contain biometric or behavioral data that can identify the child, creating identifiability risks during data transmission.

title: Child user may inappropriately store or share received video
description: The child user (EE2) may store, forward, or share the received video with unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of personal data.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations by child user
description: The child user may not comply with applicable data protection and privacy regulations when receiving and handling the video data, creating regulatory compliance risks.

title: Explicit disclosure of child browsing data to AI engine
description: Child browsing data is explicitly transferred from MongoDB collection to AI Recommendation Engine. This disclosure may violate minimality principle if the data is not strictly required for the AI's intended purpose. The AI engine may process, store, or use this data in ways that extend beyond the original collection purpose.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the AI engine is a third-party or external system; if it's internal, risk may be lower but still present.

title: Linkability of child data in transit
description: Child browsing data transmitted between MongoDB and AI engine may contain metadata or patterns that allow linking of browsing behavior to specific children or households. This could enable profiling or tracking across systems.
uncertainty_note: Depends on data format and whether metadata is stripped during transmission.

title: Identification of children through AI processing
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may process child browsing data in ways that enable identification of individual children, either directly or through inference from browsing patterns. This could lead to unintended identification beyond the original data collection purpose.
uncertainty_note: Depends on AI engine's processing capabilities and data retention policies.

title: Source element sharing child data without adequate consent validation
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection may share child browsing data without verifying that appropriate parental consent or legal basis exists for this specific disclosure to the AI engine. The source element's act of sharing causes the threat.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard data governance practices; actual risk depends on consent management system.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) explicitly transfers browsing data to third-party advertisers (EE3) as part of its planned functionality. This represents an intentional disclosure of personal data across a system boundary, which may violate the minimality principle if the data shared is not strictly required for the advertising purpose.

title: Linkability via Browsing Data in Transit
description: Browsing data transmitted in the DF14 flow may contain metadata or patterns that allow third parties to link the data to specific users or sessions, potentially enabling cross-referencing with other data sources.

title: Uncontrolled Data Processing by Advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers (EE3) receive browsing data and may process, store, or share it in ways that exceed the original purpose of the disclosure, potentially leading to further unintended data disclosures.

title: Identification Risk During Data Transfer
description: The browsing data transmitted in this flow may contain personally identifiable information or quasi-identifiers that could be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Government ID Images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system backend/uploads/ are sensitive personal data. If the data store is not properly secured, unauthorized parties could access, view, or copy these images, leading to explicit data disclosure. This violates the minimality principle as the data is stored beyond what may be strictly necessary for authentication purposes.
assumptions: The file system lacks adequate access controls, encryption at rest, or audit logging for the stored ID images.

title: Data Disclosure During Transfer to File System
description: Government ID images in transit from the Authentication Service to the file system could be intercepted or logged by network monitoring tools, creating implicit disclosure through metadata or network traffic analysis.
assumptions: The data transfer may not use end-to-end encryption or secure protocols.

title: Identification Risk from Stored Government ID Images
description: Government ID images contain biometric and personal identifying information. Storing these images in the file system creates a persistent identification risk, as the images can be used to identify individuals even if other authentication data is compromised.
assumptions: The stored images are not properly anonymized or access-controlled.

title: Unnecessary Collection and Storage of Government ID Images
description: The Authentication Service may be collecting and storing government ID images beyond what is strictly necessary for authentication purposes, violating the minimality principle. If authentication can be achieved through other means (e.g., token-based), storing full ID images is excessive.
assumptions: The authentication process requires full ID image storage rather than just verification.

title: JWT contains user identifiers exposed at source
description: The Authentication Service shares a JWT that contains user identifiers (user ID, session ID, etc.). The act of sharing this data at the source element exposes personally identifiable information to the data flow.

title: JWT stored in localStorage accessible to any JavaScript
description: Browser localStorage makes stored data accessible to any JavaScript running on the page. This creates a disclosure risk where the JWT (containing sensitive authentication data) can be read by malicious scripts or compromised code.

title: localStorage vulnerable to XSS attacks
description: Browser localStorage is vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. An attacker with XSS access can read, modify, or steal the stored JWT, leading to session hijacking and unauthorized access to user accounts.

title: Flow metadata could link authentication events
description: Metadata about the data flow (source P1, destination DS5, timing, volume) could be used to link authentication events across sessions or correlate user activity patterns, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.
uncertainty_note: Less certain - depends on whether metadata is actually exposed or observable

title: Child data sharing enables profile linking
description: Process P3 shares child history data with parent EE1, which may contain recurring identifiers or quasi-identifiers that allow linking of the child's information with other data sources, potentially building a comprehensive profile beyond the intended scope.

title: Metadata in data flow enables identification
description: Data in transit (DF17) may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, request patterns, or identifiers) that could be used to link or identify the child or parent, even if the payload itself is protected.

title: Parent can link child data with external information
description: Parent user EE1, upon receiving child history data, may combine it with external information (e.g., social media, other services) to build a more detailed profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond the intended review scope.

title: Child identifiable information disclosed to parent
description: The child history data may contain personally identifiable information about the child that, while intended for the parent, could be misused or shared further, leading to unintended identification of the child to third parties.
